title: Gas exchange system diagram
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: The periodic table (8F); breathing and respiration (8C)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 35 (Gas exchange system diagram (portal worksheet, printable or on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 35: The gas exchange system. To understand how the structure of the lungs is adapted for gas exchange

picture.alt: A diagram of the gas exchange system
picture.draw: Draw and label: Gas exchange system diagram

questions.q: Explain why a large surface area helps the lungs.
questions.a: More oxygen can diffuse into the blood at the same time, so gas exchange is faster
questions.model: What happens across the surface? Diffusion. More surface, more places for diffusion at once. So faster gas exchange.

questions.q: Which way does carbon dioxide diffuse in the lungs?
questions.a: From the blood into the alveoli

questions.q: Label the gas exchange system diagram and, on the alveolus close-up, draw arrows for oxygen and carbon dioxide.
questions.a: Correct labels; oxygen arrow alveolus to capillary; CO₂ arrow capillary to alveolus
questions.model: Teacher labels the trachea first and adds the oxygen arrow.

questions.q: Use the term concentration gradient to explain why breathing keeps gas exchange going.
questions.a: Breathing brings fresh air in and removes CO₂, keeping oxygen high in alveoli and low in blood.

questions.q: Emphysema destroys alveolus walls, making fewer, larger sacs. Explain why patients are breathless.
questions.a: Smaller surface area, so less oxygen diffuses into the blood.

questions.q: Gases cross the alveolus wall by...
Big question: why do lungs need such a huge surface?
questions.a: So enough oxygen diffuses into the blood quickly.
